title: SSE stream fragment orphan healing and tenant-priority graceful fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Two enterprise customers have escalated intermittent truncated streaming responses from the Hosted SSE API. Symptoms: clients receive a partial sequence of tokens followed by a silent disconnect or a TCP FIN; the hosted runtime does not emit a finalization marker and downstream SDKs cannot determine whether the response is complete. Root-cause signals point to edge proxy connection preemption combined with tenant-priority multiplexing where in-flight fragments are orphaned in the stream assembler. Impact: customer app UX regressions, retries producing duplicated content or hung UI spinners, and some downstream idempotency invariants broken for function-calling flows.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted SSE emits an explicit finalization sentinel or an ordered 'fragment-fence' for every final token boundary within 250ms of connection close
No customer-visible duplicated token sequences in 99.9% of simulated preemption events (test harness) compared to baseline
Automatic fallback to non-streaming (polling/long-poll) for affected requests reduces customer error rate by >= 85% during canary windows
E2E regression tests added to runtime CI that injects midstream connection termination and asserts deterministic reassembly
steps_to_repro: 1) Use the hosted SSE endpoint with a high-verbosity generation model and tenant-priority routing enabled
2) While stream is in-flight, trigger a simulated edge preemption (proxy sends RST or connection closed) or induce a short network blackhole
3) Observe the client SDK: partial tokens received, no finalization sentinel, and then a socket close event
4) Replay with the SDK resume logic disabled to see duplication or missing tail tokens
proposed_solution: A) Introduce a lightweight per-request incarnation ID (opaque session_version) written to every fragment/event. On connection close, runtime emits a FINALIZE event that includes session_version and last-seen-offset
B) Implement server-side short-lived persistent snapshot for in-flight KV cache pointers so the reassembly worker can reconstruct final token ranges if fragments are orphaned
C) Add tenant-priority-aware fragment fencing: when preemption is detected, mark affected fragments as 'orphaned' and route them to a reconciliation backfill queue rather than dropping silently
D) SDK mitigation: expose a clear error class (SSEPartialOrphan) with recommended immediate fallback to polling mode; provide opt-in auto-fallback in SDKs behind feature flag
E) Operational: add an on-call runbook that instructs engineers to trigger the backfill worker for impacted tenant_ids and to toggle auto-fallback per-tenant
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the finalize-sentinel at runtime with default off for 100% of traffic
Canary: enable for 5% of traffic in a single region and a small subset of low-risk tenant_ids for 48 hours
Monitor metrics (see telemetry) and run synthetic replay harness against canary traffic
If stable, ramp to 25% for 24h, then 75% for 24h, then 100%
After finalize-sentinel is stable, enable SDK auto-fallback opt-in for 1% of customers and expand based on customer feedback
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Adding extra events increases stream bandwidth and subtle ordering changes could break poorly-behaved SDKs; Mitigation: keep sentinel minimal (32B) and document ordering contract
Risk: Backfill worker might re-emit fragments out-of-order; Mitigation: reconcile using log-offsets and session_version, enforce monotonic sequence check
Risk: Canaries could surface unexpected latency for tight-latency customers; Mitigation: exclude dedicated clusters with strict latency SLAs from early canaries
telemetry_and_alerting: alert: P99 stream completion latency increase > 50ms for canary cluster -> page oncall
alert: orphan_fragment_detected rate > 0.05% of requests for 5m -> create incident ticket and rollback canary
